stemMd: For an X-linked recessive trait, a carrier woman and an unaffected man have a son. Assuming equal transmission of the mother's X chromosomes, what is the chance that this son has the trait?
explanationMd: A son receives Y from his father and one X from his mother. Half the mother's X-bearing eggs carry the recessive allele, so half of sons are expected to express it under the stated model.

distractorRationale.b: That includes the separate probability of having a son, which is already given.
distractorRationale.d: This is not the segregation ratio for a son in this cross.
distractorRationale.e: A carrier mother also has a non-mutant X chromosome.
distractorRationale.a: An unaffected father does not protect sons from a maternal X allele.
